facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a genus of duck-billed dinosaur with a name meaning "hooked-nosed lizard" in Greek.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus (meaning "hooked-nosed (Greek grypos) lizard"; sometimes incorrectly translated as "griffin (Latin gryphus) lizard") was a genus of duckbilled dinosaur

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived approximately 80 to 75 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in North America.
facts.quote: lived about 80 to 75 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous (late Santonian to late Campanian stages) of North America

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is distinguished from other duck-billed dinosaurs by a narrow, arching nasal hump resembling a Roman nose.
facts.quote: It is most easily distinguished from other duckbills by its narrow arching nasal hump, sometimes described as similar to a "Roman nose,"

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a large herbivore that could walk on two or four legs and measured around 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: A large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore around 8 m long, it may have preferred river settings.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence includes skin impressions showing pyramidal scales projecting along the midline of Gryposaurus's back.
facts.quote: It is known from numerous skulls, some skeletons, and even some skin impressions that show it to have had pyramidal scales projecting along the midline of the back.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe described and named Gryposaurus shortly after its discovery, highlighting its unusual nasal crest.
facts.quote: This specimen was described and named by Lawrence Lambe shortly thereafter, Lambe drawing attention to its unusual nasal crest.

facts.statement: William Parks named a skeleton Kritosaurus incurvimanus rather than Gryposaurus incurvimanus, reflecting the historical debate over whether the two genera were the same.
facts.quote: This idea was reflected in William Parks's naming of a nearly complete skeleton from the Dinosaur Park Formation as Kritosaurus incurvimanus, not Gryposaurus incurvimanus

facts.statement: Current research distinguishes Hadrosaurus from Gryposaurus based on differences in the upper arm and ilium, despite past hypotheses linking them.
facts.quote: Current thought is that Hadrosaurus, although known from fragmentary material, can be distinguished from Gryposaurus by differences in the upper arm and ilium.

facts.statement: The informal name "Hadrosauravus" was an early, unused name for the species Gryposaurus latidens.
facts.quote: The informal name "Hadrosauravus" is an early, unused name for this species.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Gryposaurus have been found in the El Picacho Formation in Texas.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of Gryposaurus have also been unearthed in the El Picacho Formation in Texas.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Gryposaurus notabilis represents an animal approximately 8.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: one of the best specimens of this genus, the nearly complete type specimen of Kritosaurus incurvimanus (now regarded as a synonym of Gryposaurus notabilis) came from an animal about 8.2 m long.

facts.statement: Skin impressions reveal that Gryposaurus had scutes up to 3.8 centimeters long on its flanks and tail.
facts.quote: showing this dinosaur to have had several different types of scalation: pyramidal, ridged, limpet-shaped feature scales forming scutes upwards of 3.8 centimeters long (1.5 inches) on the flank and tail

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Gryposaurus latidens to be 7.5 meters long with a body mass of 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated the size of G. latidens at 7.5 m in length and 2.5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Gryposaurus notabilis and G. monumentensis to be 8 meters long with a body mass of 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: the other two species (G. notabilis and G. monumentensis) at 8 m in length and 3 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The prominent nasal arch of Gryposaurus is formed by the paired nasal bones.
facts.quote: The prominent nasal arch found in this genus is formed from the paired nasal bones.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a type of duckbill dinosaur without hollow head crests.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus was a saurolophine (hadrosaurine of older references) hadrosaurid, a member of the duckbill subfamily without hollow head crests.

facts.statement: Jack Horner coined the subfamily Gryposaurinae, but this classification is no longer in use.
facts.quote: A subfamily, Gryposaurinae, was coined by Jack Horner as part of a larger revision that promoted Hadrosaurinae to family status, but is not now in use.

facts.statement: The genus Gryposaurus was named by Lambe in 1914.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lambe, 1914

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gryposaurus is Gryposaurus notabilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Gryposaurus notabilis

facts.statement: Known species include Gryposaurus latidens (Horner, 1992), Gryposaurus monumentensis (Gates & Sampson, 2007), and the dubious Gryposaurus alsatei (Lehman, Wick, Wagner, 2016).
facts.quote: subdivision: Gryposaurus latidens Horner, 1992 Gryposaurus monumentensis Gates & Sampson, 2007 Gryposaurus alsatei? Lehman, Wick, Wagner, 2016

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived between 85 and 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del periodo Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 85 y 66 millones de años, entre el Santoniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The type species Gryposaurus notabilis is from the Late Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: la especie tipo es Gryposaurus notabilis de la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta, Canadá, del Campaniense tardío

facts.statement: Gryposaurus latidens is from the Santonian Dos Medicinas Formation of Montana, USA.
facts.quote: la segunda especie nombrada fue Gryposaurus latidens de la Formación Dos Medicina del Santoniense de Montana, EE. UU.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus monumentensis is from the Campanian Kaiparowits Formation of Utah, USA.
facts.quote: la tercera especie considerada válida es Gryposaurus monumentensis de la Formación Kaiparowits en Utah, EE. UU. también del Campaniense.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus alsatei is from the Late Maastrichtian Javelina Formation of Texas, USA, but is considered dubious.
facts.quote: Por último la especie Gryposaurus alsatei de la Formación Javelina en Texas EE. UU., que data del Maastrichtiense tardío, siendo considerada dudosa.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore that ate a variety of plants.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Gryposaurus would have been a bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating a variety of plants.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus had skull joints allowing a grinding motion and dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at once.
facts.quote: Its skull had special joints that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus could feed on plants ranging from the ground up to about 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Its feeding range would have extended from the ground to about 4 m above.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Gryposaurus was both a grazer and a browser, eating tough, fibrous plant material.
facts.quote: The paleontologists who unearthed G. monumentensis back in the 2000s brought the fact that this creature dined on tough, fibrous plant material which would imply that Gryposaurs was both a grazer and a browser.

facts.statement: Because only one specimen was analyzed, the feeding patterns inferred from its dental microwear may not represent the whole taxon.
facts.quote: However, because only one specimen had dental microwear texture analysis performed on it, this may not reflect the overall feeding patterns of this taxon.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus may have preferred habitats related to rivers.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus may have preferred river-related settings.

facts.statement: The distinctive nasal arch of Gryposaurus may have been used for social functions like identifying sex, species, or social ranking.
facts.quote: The distinctive nasal arch of Gryposaurus, like other cranial modifications in duckbills, may have been used for a variety of social functions, such as identification of sexes or species and social ranking.

facts.statement: The nasal arch may have been used for pushing or butting in contests, possibly flanked by inflatable air sacs for signaling.
facts.quote: It could also have functioned as a tool for broadside pushing or butting in social contests, and there may have been inflatable air sacs flanking it for both visual and auditory signaling.

facts.statement: Argon-argon dating places the deposition of the Kaiparowits Formation between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Argon-argon radiometric dating indicates that the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.1 and 74.0 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Kaiparowits Formation was near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, which split North America into Laramidia and Appalachia.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous period, the site of the Kaiparowits Formation was located near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, a large inland sea that split North America into two landmasses, Laramidia to the west and Appalachia to the east.

facts.statement: The habitat was an ancient floodplain with large channels, wetland swamps, ponds, and lakes, bordered by highlands.
facts.quote: The plateau where dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetland peat swamps, ponds and lakes, and was bordered by highlands.

facts.statement: The climate was wet and humid, supporting abundant and diverse organisms.
facts.quote: The climate was wet and humid, and supported an abundant and diverse range of organisms.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus monumentensis shared its environment with dromaeosaurids, troodontids, ornithomimids, tyrannosaurids, ankylosaurids, Parasaurolophus, various ceratopsians, and Hagryphus.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus monumentensis shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as dromaeosaurid theropods, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, ornithomimids like Ornithomimus velox, tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus and Teratophoneus, armored ankylosaurids, the duckbilled hadrosaur Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus, the ceratopsians Utahceratops gettyi, Nasutoceratops titusi and Kosmoceratops richardsoni and the oviraptorosaurian Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: Other fauna in the Kaiparowits Formation included sharks, rays, frogs, salamanders, turtles, lizards, and crocodilians.
facts.quote: Other paleofauna present in the Kaiparowits Formation included chondrichthyans (sharks and rays), frogs, salamanders, turtles, lizards and crocodilians.

facts.statement: Early mammals present included multituberculates, marsupials, and insectivorans.
facts.quote: A variety of early mammals were present including multituberculates, marsupials, and insectivorans.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is distinguished by a narrow nasal arch sometimes described as a "Roman nose," possibly used for species identification or combat.
facts.quote: Se distingue más fácilmente de otros dinosaurios de pico de pato por su gancho nasal de arco estrecho, que a veces se describe como similar a la " nariz romana " y que puede haber sido utilizada para la identificación de especies o sexual y combate con individuos de la misma especie. especies.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a large herbivore about 9 meters long that could move bipedally or quadrupedally and preferred living near rivers.
facts.quote: Fue un gran herbívoro que podía avanzar de forma bípeda como cuadrúpeda de alrededor de 9 metros de largo, que preferiría vivir junto a los ríos.

facts.statement: Numerous skulls, skeletons, and skin impressions show Gryposaurus had pyramidal scales projecting along the midline of the back.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de numerosos cráneos, algunos esqueletos e incluso algunas impresiones de la piel que muestran que tenían escamas piramidales que se proyectan a lo largo de la línea media de la espalda.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the tribe Gryposaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Gryposaurini

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Saurolophinae

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is a genus of dinosaurs.
facts.quote: genus: Gryposaurus

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the kingdom Animalia.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the phylum Chordata.
facts.quote: phylum: Chordata

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the class Sauropsida.
facts.quote: classis: Sauropsida

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the superorder Dinosauria.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the order Ornithischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Ornithischia

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kritosaurus is a synonym of Gryposaurus, though Kritosaurus is slightly younger.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus has been proposed to be a synonym of Gryposaurus, but it is slightly younger.

facts.statement: "Hadrosauravus" is listed as a synonym of Gryposaurus but is considered a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: synonyms: "Hadrosauravus" (nomen nudum) Lambert, 1990

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a typical-sized hadrosaurid measuring approximately 9 meters long and 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus era un hadrosaúrido de tamaño y forma típicos, medía aproximadamente 9 metros de largo y 4 de alto.

facts.statement: The most robust known species, G. monumentensis, may have reached 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: De las cuatro especies conocidas la más robusta es G. monumentensis que puede haber llegado a los 10 metros.

facts.statement: A nearly complete specimen shows skin impressions including pyramidal scales, grooved scales, and shell-like shields over 3.8 centimeters long on the flank and tail.
facts.quote: Este espécimen también tiene el mejor ejemplo de impresiones de piel para Gryposaurus , mostrando que este dinosaurio ha tenido varios tipos diferentes de escamación, piramidal, acanalada, escudos como lapa de más de 3,8 centímetros de largo en el flanco y la cola.

facts.statement: The prominent nasal arch forms a rounded hump in front of the eyes that reaches the same height as the back of the skull.
facts.quote: El arco nasal prominente que se encuentra en este género se forma a partir de los huesos nasales pareados . En vista de perfil, se elevan en una joroba redondeada delante de los ojos, alcanzando una altura tan alta como el punto más alto de la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus had one of the highest numbers of teeth among dinosaurs, with about 300 active teeth and nearly 800 including replacement teeth.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus exhiben uno de los mayores números de dientes entre los dinosaurios, presentando unos 300 activos y en total cerca de 800 si se cuentan los de reemplazo.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the nasal arch held an air-filled skin sac used for social communication, with males possibly changing color and blood flow during mating season.
facts.quote: El típico arco nasal del Gryposaurus, del que se cree que sostuvo una bolsa de piel la cual podía llenar de aire para hacerla sonar, tuvo una función social de comunicación dentro de la manada y también se especula que los machos en época de apareamiento se exhibían subiendo el tono del color, aumentando así su irrigación.

facts.statement: The genus Gryposaurus is based on specimen NMC 2278, found in 1913 by George F. Sternberg in the Dinosaur Park Formation along the Red Deer River.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus está basado en el ejemplar NMC 2278, encontrado en 1913 por George F. Sternberg en la Formación Dinosaur Park en el Río Red Deer.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe described the specimen, noting the distinctive nasal arch.
facts.quote: Este espécimen fue descrito por Lawrence Lambe, donde le llamó la atención el arco nasal.

facts.statement: A 1942 monograph by Lull and Wright established synonymy between Kritosaurus and Gryposaurus for nearly fifty years, favoring Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: La publicación de 1942 de la influyente monografía de Lull y Wright sobre los hadrosáuridos selló la cuestión de la sinonimia entre Kritosaurus y Gryposaurus por casi cincuenta años a favor de Kritosaurus.

facts.statement: New material from the Kaiparowits Formation in Utah, including a skull and partial skeleton, was named G. monumentensis.
facts.quote: Un nuevo material de la Formación Kaiparowits en Utah, del Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, que incluye cráneo y esqueleto parcial, es llamado G. monumentensis.

facts.statement: The type species G. notabilis lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: La especie tipo G. notabilis es del Campaniense tardío en el Cretácico superior de la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: G. latidens lived during the Santonian stage in the Dos Medicinas Formation of Pondera County, Montana, USA.
facts.quote: G. latidens , del Santoniense, en la formación Formación Dos Medicinas del condado de Pondera, Montana, EE. UU.

facts.statement: G. monumentensis is known from a skull and partial skeleton found in Utah.
facts.quote: G. monumentensis es conocido por un cráneo y un esqueleto parcial de Utah.

facts.statement: A possible fourth species, G. alsatei, was recently unearthed in the Javelina Formation dating to the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Recientemente, una posible cuarta especie de Gryposaurus, G. alsatei, fue desenterrada en la Formación Javelina, que data del Maastrichtiense tardío

facts.statement: As of 2016, three named species are recognized as valid: G. notabilis, G. latidens, and G. monumentensis.
facts.quote: A partir de 2016 hay tres especies nombradas que se reconocen como válidas, G. notabilis, G. latidens y G. monumentensis.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus incurvimanus is now considered a synonym of G. notabilis.
facts.quote: Ahora se piensa que otra especie de la misma formación, Kritosaurus incurvimanus, también conocida como Gryposaurus incurvimanus, es un sinónimo de G. notabilis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the dubious Alberta dinosaur originally named Trachodon (Pteropelyx) marginatus should be included in G. notabilis, though this has not been formally reported.
facts.quote: El dinosaurio dudoso de Alberta originalmente llamado Trachodon (Pteropelyx) marginatus por Lambe en 1902, que fuera incluido en Kritosaurus, debería ser incluido en G. notabilis pero todavía no ha sido informado correctamente.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is a saurolophine hadrosaurid, an older-referencing hadrosaurine, and a member of the crestless duck-billed subfamily.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus es un hadrosáurido saurolofino, hadrosaurino de referencias más antiguas, un miembro de la subfamilia de pico de pato sin crestas de cabeza hueca.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is most closely related to the dinosaur Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Entre los dinosaurios con los que se encuentra más cercano está el Kritosaurus.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus comes from rocks that are slightly younger than those containing Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus proviene de rocas levemente más jóvenes que Gryposaurus.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus fossils are found in Alberta and Montana, while Kritosaurus fossils are found in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Alberta y Montana para Gryposaurus, Nuevo México para Kritosaurus

facts.statement: The Kritosaurus skull is largely incomplete, missing most facial bones, but is very similar to that of Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: Aparte, la calavera de Kritosaurus no es completamente conocida, faltándole la mayoría de los huesos del rostro pero es muy similar a la del Gryposaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Gryposaurus is the tribe Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Kritosaurini

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: As a hadrosaurid, Gryposaurus was likely a herbivore that could walk on two or four legs and ate a variety of plants.
facts.quote: Como hadrosáurido, Gryposaurus habría sido un herbívoro que podía andar en dos o cuatro patas, que comía una variedad de plantas.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus had special skull joints allowing abrasive chewing-like movement, and its teeth were continuously replaced and packed into batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a handful in use at any time.
facts.quote: Su cráneo tenía articulaciones especiales que permitían un movimiento abrasivo análogo al de masticar y sus dientes se reemplazaban y empaquetaban continuamente en baterías dentales que contenían cientos de dientes, solo un puñado relativo de los cuales estaban en uso al mismo tiempo.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus likely used its wide beak to crop vegetation and cheek-like organs to hold food in its jaws.
facts.quote: El material vegetal habría sido recortado por su ancho pico, y sostenido en las mandíbulas por un órgano similar a una mejilla.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus' feeding range likely extended from the ground up to about 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Su rango de alimentación se habría extendido desde el suelo hasta unos 4 metros por encima.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus may have chosen to live in areas near rivers.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus puede haber elegido una zona junto al río para vivir.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus' distinctive nasal arch may have been used for social functions such as identifying sex or species and social classification.
facts.quote: El arco nasal distintivo de Gryposaurus, al igual que otras modificaciones craneales en los picos de pato, puede haber sido utilizado para una variedad de funciones sociales, como la identificación de sexos o especies y la clasificación social.

facts.statement: The nasal arch could have functioned as a tool for pushing or striking in social combat, and inflatable air sacs may have flanked it for visual and auditory signaling.
facts.quote: También podría haber funcionado como una herramienta para empujar o golpear en combates sociales, y puede haber habido bolsas de aire inflables que lo flanquean tanto para la señalización visual como auditiva.

facts.statement: The top of the nasal arch is rough in some specimens, suggesting it was covered by thick keratinized skin or had a cartilaginous extension.
facts.quote: La parte superior del arco está rugosa en algunos especímenes, lo que sugiere que estaba cubierta por una piel gruesa y queratinizada o que había una extensión cartilaginosa.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros was once thought to belong to the Gryposaurus genus before being described, when it was known by the nickname "Antonio".
facts.quote: Se pensó una vez que Tethyshadros también formaba parte de este género, antes de que fuera descrito, entonces conocido bajo el apodo de "Antonio".

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 22
